##grey fantail and tumba environ metrics combined

```{r}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Tumbarumba: Grey Fantail activity and environmental conditions
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Scientific investigation
#
# Is Grey Fantail vocal activity associated with temperature
# anomalies at Tumbarumba?
#
# First combine acoustic activity with air temperature,
# soil temperature and soil moisture.
#
# Use monthly summaries to investigate ecological patterns.

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Select Tumbarumba Grey Fantail acoustic records
# ------------------------------------------------------------

tumba_birds <- grey_activity %>%
  filter(site == "Tumbarumba01") %>%
  mutate(month = floor_date(date, "month")) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(
    vocal_windows = sum(vocal_windows),
    total_windows = sum(total_windows),
    vocal_activity = 100 * vocal_windows / total_windows,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Calculate monthly environmental conditions
# ------------------------------------------------------------

monthly_environment <- function(data, measurement, output_name) {

  data %>%
    filter(
      grepl("Tumbarumba", site_name, ignore.case = TRUE),
      as.Date(start_date_time) >= tumba_start,
      as.Date(start_date_time) <= tumba_end
    ) %>%
    mutate(month = floor_date(as.Date(start_date_time), "month")) %>%
    group_by(month) %>%
    summarise(
      value = if (all(is.na(.data[[measurement]])))
        NA_real_
      else mean(.data[[measurement]], na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    rename(!!output_name := value)
}

tumba_air <- monthly_environment(
  GERI_airtemperature_30min,
  "mean_air_temp_degC",
  "air_temperature"
)

tumba_soil_temp <- monthly_environment(
  GERI_soiltemperature_30min,
  "mean_soil_temp_degC",
  "soil_temperature"
)

tumba_soil_moisture <- monthly_environment(
  GERI_soilmoisture_30min,
  "mean_swc_percent",
  "soil_moisture"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Combine acoustic and environmental measurements
# ------------------------------------------------------------

tumba_combined <- tumba_birds %>%
  left_join(tumba_air, by = "month") %>%
  left_join(tumba_soil_temp, by = "month") %>%
  left_join(tumba_soil_moisture, by = "month") %>%
  mutate(calendar_month = month(month))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Calculate temperature anomalies
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Anomalies represent departures from the average
# temperature for the same calendar month during 2012–2019.

tumba_combined <- tumba_combined %>%
  group_by(calendar_month) %>%
  mutate(
    air_anomaly = air_temperature -
      mean(air_temperature, na.rm = TRUE),
    soil_anomaly = soil_temperature -
      mean(soil_temperature, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Plot vocal activity against air temperature anomalies
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggplot(
  tumba_combined,
  aes(x = air_anomaly, y = vocal_activity)
) +
  geom_point(
    colour = "steelblue",
    size = 2,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = TRUE,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Tumbarumba: Grey Fantail vocal activity",
    subtitle = "Relationship with monthly air temperature anomalies",
    x = "Air temperature anomaly (°C)",
    y = "Vocal activity (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(colour = "black")
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Questions for interpretation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Does vocal activity increase or decrease during
#    warmer-than-average months?
#
# 2. Is the relationship approximately linear?
#
# 3. Could soil temperature or moisture show stronger
#    relationships with vocal activity?
#
# 4. Does the relationship persist after accounting
#    statistically for seasonality?

```
##model test of grey fantail at Tumba

```{r}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Tumbarumba: modelling Grey Fantail vocal activity
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Scientific investigation
#
# Does Grey Fantail vocal activity vary seasonally?
#
# Do air temperature, soil temperature and soil moisture
# anomalies explain additional variation after accounting
# for season?
#
# Response:
# Number of 3-second windows containing vocalisations,
# relative to the total number of recorded windows.
#
# Models:
# 1. Season only
# 2. Season + environmental anomalies
#
# These are exploratory associations, not causal tests.

library(dplyr)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare the modelling dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Calculate soil moisture anomalies relative to the
# average for each calendar month during 2012–2019.

tumba_model_data <- tumba_combined %>%
  group_by(calendar_month) %>%
  mutate(
    moisture_anomaly = soil_moisture -
      mean(soil_moisture, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    season = factor(
      case_when(
        calendar_month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Summer",
        calendar_month %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "Autumn",
        calendar_month %in% c(6, 7, 8) ~ "Winter",
        TRUE ~ "Spring"
      ),
      levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Autumn")
    ),
    non_vocal_windows = total_windows - vocal_windows
  ) %>%
  filter(
    complete.cases(
      air_anomaly,
      soil_anomaly,
      moisture_anomaly,
      season
    ),
    total_windows > 0,
    vocal_windows >= 0,
    non_vocal_windows >= 0
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Fit the season-only model
# ------------------------------------------------------------

model_season <- glm(
  cbind(vocal_windows, non_vocal_windows) ~ season,
  family = quasibinomial(link = "logit"),
  data = tumba_model_data
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Fit the season + environment model
# ------------------------------------------------------------

model_environment <- glm(
  cbind(vocal_windows, non_vocal_windows) ~
    season +
    air_anomaly +
    soil_anomaly +
    moisture_anomaly,
  family = quasibinomial(link = "logit"),
  data = tumba_model_data
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Compare the two models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\nMODEL COMPARISON\n\n")

print(
  anova(
    model_season,
    model_environment,
    test = "F"
  )
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Examine the full model
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\nFULL MODEL RESULTS\n\n")

print(summary(model_environment))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Check overdispersion
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\nDISPERSION ESTIMATE\n\n")

print(summary(model_environment)$dispersion)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Check correlations between environmental predictors
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\nENVIRONMENTAL PREDICTOR CORRELATIONS\n\n")

print(
  round(
    cor(
      tumba_model_data %>%
        select(
          air_anomaly,
          soil_anomaly,
          moisture_anomaly
        )
    ),
    2
  )
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Report the sample size
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\nNUMBER OF MONTHS INCLUDED:\n")
print(nrow(tumba_model_data))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Questions for interpretation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Does the environmental model improve upon the
#    season-only model?
#
# 2. Which environmental predictors have statistically
#    supported associations with vocal activity?
#
# 3. Are the environmental predictors strongly correlated?
#
# 4. Is there substantial overdispersion?
#
# 5. Could temporal autocorrelation or differences in
#    recording schedules influence the results?

```

```{r}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Tumbarumba: Grey Fantail model diagnostics and coefficients
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Scientific investigation
#
# How well does the environmental model fit the acoustic data?
#
# Are environmental predictors strongly correlated?
#
# Which predictors show positive or negative associations
# with Grey Fantail vocal activity?
#
# Model coefficients are on the log-odds scale.
# Confidence intervals are exploratory given the
# substantial overdispersion observed in the model.

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Correlations between environmental predictors
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\nENVIRONMENTAL PREDICTOR CORRELATIONS\n\n")

predictor_correlations <- cor(
  tumba_model_data %>%
    select(air_anomaly, soil_anomaly, moisture_anomaly),
  use = "complete.obs"
)

print(round(predictor_correlations, 2))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Model fit statistics
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\nMODEL FIT\n\n")

model_fit <- data.frame(
  model = c("Season only", "Season + environment"),
  residual_deviance = c(
    deviance(model_season),
    deviance(model_environment)
  ),
  residual_df = c(
    df.residual(model_season),
    df.residual(model_environment)
  ),
  dispersion = c(
    summary(model_season)$dispersion,
    summary(model_environment)$dispersion
  )
)

print(model_fit, row.names = FALSE)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Residual diagnostics
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Examine whether residuals show systematic patterns.
# Large residuals or structure may indicate poor fit.

diagnostic_data <- data.frame(
  month = tumba_model_data$month,
  fitted_activity = 100 * fitted(model_environment),
  residual = residuals(model_environment, type = "pearson")
)

p_residuals <- ggplot(
  diagnostic_data,
  aes(x = fitted_activity, y = residual)
) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue", size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Model diagnostics: residuals versus fitted values",
    x = "Fitted vocal activity (%)",
    y = "Pearson residual"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(colour = "black")
  )

print(p_residuals)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Check residuals through time
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_time <- ggplot(
  diagnostic_data,
  aes(x = month, y = residual)
) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue", size = 2) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Model diagnostics: residuals through time",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Pearson residual"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(colour = "black")
  )

print(p_time)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Extract model coefficients and confidence intervals
# ------------------------------------------------------------

coefficient_table <- as.data.frame(
  summary(model_environment)$coefficients
)

coefficient_table$term <- rownames(coefficient_table)

names(coefficient_table)[1:4] <- c(
  "estimate", "std_error", "statistic", "p_value"
)

# Calculate approximate 95% confidence intervals
# using the quasibinomial model's t distribution.

critical_value <- qt(
  0.975,
  df = df.residual(model_environment)
)

coefficient_table <- coefficient_table %>%
  mutate(
    lower = estimate - critical_value * std_error,
    upper = estimate + critical_value * std_error
  ) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    predictor = recode(
      term,
      "seasonSpring" = "Spring vs winter",
      "seasonSummer" = "Summer vs winter",
      "seasonAutumn" = "Autumn vs winter",
      "air_anomaly" = "Air temperature anomaly (°C)",
      "soil_anomaly" = "Soil temperature anomaly (°C)",
      "moisture_anomaly" = "Soil moisture anomaly (%)"
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Coefficient plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_coefficients <- ggplot(
  coefficient_table,
  aes(
    x = estimate,
    y = reorder(predictor, estimate)
  )
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey50"
  ) +
  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper),
    height = 0.2,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = 3,
    colour = "steelblue"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Grey Fantail: seasonal and environmental associations",
    subtitle = "Quasibinomial model, approximate 95% confidence intervals",
    x = "Model coefficient (log-odds)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(colour = "black"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(p_coefficients)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Questions for interpretation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Do the residuals show systematic patterns?
#
# 2. Is there evidence of temporal dependence?
#
# 3. Does the model show substantial overdispersion?
#
# 4. Which coefficient confidence intervals exclude zero?
#
# 5. Are the results robust enough for ecological inference?

```

```{r}

# ============================================================
# Tumbarumba: Grey Fantail vocal activity and environment
# Beta regression analysis
# ============================================================

# Scientific investigation
#
# Does Grey Fantail vocal activity vary with season?
#
# Do air temperature anomalies, soil temperature anomalies
# and soil moisture anomalies explain additional variation
# after accounting for season?
#
# Beta regression treats each monthly vocal activity
# proportion as an observation, rather than treating
# every 3-second acoustic window as independent.
#
# The analysis is exploratory and does not establish
# causal relationships.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load packages
# ------------------------------------------------------------

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

if (!requireNamespace("betareg", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("betareg")
}

library(betareg)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Prepare monthly vocal activity proportions
# ------------------------------------------------------------

tumba_beta_data <- tumba_model_data %>%
  mutate(
    vocal_proportion = vocal_windows / total_windows
  ) %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(vocal_proportion),
    vocal_proportion > 0,
    vocal_proportion < 1,
    complete.cases(
      season,
      air_anomaly,
      soil_anomaly,
      moisture_anomaly
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(month)

cat("\nNUMBER OF MONTHS INCLUDED:\n")
print(nrow(tumba_beta_data))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Fit season-only model
# ------------------------------------------------------------

beta_season <- betareg(
  vocal_proportion ~ season,
  data = tumba_beta_data,
  link = "logit"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Fit season + environment model
# ------------------------------------------------------------

beta_environment <- betareg(
  vocal_proportion ~
    season +
    air_anomaly +
    soil_anomaly +
    moisture_anomaly,
  data = tumba_beta_data,
  link = "logit"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Compare the two models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Likelihood-ratio test for nested beta regression models.

loglik_season <- logLik(beta_season)
loglik_environment <- logLik(beta_environment)

lr_statistic <- 2 * (
  as.numeric(loglik_environment) -
    as.numeric(loglik_season)
)

df_difference <- attr(loglik_environment, "df") -
  attr(loglik_season, "df")

p_value <- pchisq(
  lr_statistic,
  df = df_difference,
  lower.tail = FALSE
)

cat("\nMODEL COMPARISON\n\n")

print(
  data.frame(
    likelihood_ratio = lr_statistic,
    degrees_of_freedom = df_difference,
    p_value = p_value
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Model fit statistics
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\nMODEL FIT STATISTICS\n\n")

model_fit <- data.frame(
  model = c("Season only", "Season + environment"),
  AIC = c(
    AIC(beta_season),
    AIC(beta_environment)
  ),
  BIC = c(
    BIC(beta_season),
    BIC(beta_environment)
  ),
  pseudo_R2 = c(
    summary(beta_season)$pseudo.r.squared,
    summary(beta_environment)$pseudo.r.squared
  )
)

print(model_fit, row.names = FALSE)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Full model results
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\nBETA REGRESSION RESULTS\n\n")

print(summary(beta_environment))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Environmental predictor correlations
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\nENVIRONMENTAL PREDICTOR CORRELATIONS\n\n")

print(
  round(
    cor(
      tumba_beta_data %>%
        select(
          air_anomaly,
          soil_anomaly,
          moisture_anomaly
        )
    ),
    2
  )
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Residual diagnostics
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Standardised weighted residuals help identify observations
# that are poorly predicted by the model.

diagnostic_data <- data.frame(
  month = tumba_beta_data$month,
  fitted_activity = 100 * fitted(beta_environment),
  residual = as.numeric(
    residuals(beta_environment, type = "sweighted2")
  )
)

p_residuals <- ggplot(
  diagnostic_data,
  aes(x = fitted_activity, y = residual)
) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue", size = 2) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Beta regression: residuals versus fitted values",
    x = "Fitted vocal activity (%)",
    y = "Standardised weighted residual"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(colour = "black")
  )

print(p_residuals)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Residuals through time
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_time <- ggplot(
  diagnostic_data,
  aes(x = month, y = residual)
) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue", size = 1.5) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Beta regression: residuals through time",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Standardised weighted residual"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(colour = "black")
  )

print(p_time)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Extract mean-model coefficients
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Coefficients are on the logit scale.
# Confidence intervals use the model's standard errors.

coefficient_table <- as.data.frame(
  summary(beta_environment)$coefficients$mean
)

coefficient_table$term <- rownames(coefficient_table)

names(coefficient_table)[1:4] <- c(
  "estimate",
  "std_error",
  "statistic",
  "p_value"
)

coefficient_table <- coefficient_table %>%
  mutate(
    lower = estimate - 1.96 * std_error,
    upper = estimate + 1.96 * std_error
  ) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    predictor = recode(
      term,
      "seasonSpring" = "Spring vs winter",
      "seasonSummer" = "Summer vs winter",
      "seasonAutumn" = "Autumn vs winter",
      "air_anomaly" = "Air temperature anomaly (°C)",
      "soil_anomaly" = "Soil temperature anomaly (°C)",
      "moisture_anomaly" = "Soil moisture anomaly (%)"
    )
  )

cat("\nCOEFFICIENT ESTIMATES\n\n")

print(
  coefficient_table %>%
    select(
      predictor,
      estimate,
      lower,
      upper,
      p_value
    ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 12. Coefficient plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_coefficients <- ggplot(
  coefficient_table,
  aes(
    x = estimate,
    y = reorder(predictor, estimate)
  )
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey50"
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper),
    orientation = "y",
    width = 0.2,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = 3,
    colour = "steelblue"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Grey Fantail: seasonal and environmental associations",
    subtitle = "Beta regression with approximate 95% confidence intervals",
    x = "Model coefficient (log-odds)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(colour = "black"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(p_coefficients)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 13. Questions for interpretation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Does adding environmental variables improve model fit
#    beyond season alone?
#
# 2. Which model has the lower AIC?
#
# 3. Is soil temperature positively associated with
#    Grey Fantail vocal activity in the beta regression?
#
# 4. Do residuals show systematic patterns or outliers?
#
# 5. Is there evidence of temporal autocorrelation?
#
# 6. Are the coefficient confidence intervals narrower
#    than those from the quasibinomial model?
#
# IMPORTANT:
# Beta regression avoids treating every acoustic window
# as an independent binomial trial, but it does not
# automatically account for temporal autocorrelation,
# variation in recording effort or other dependencies.
#
# Interpret statistical associations cautiously.
```

#screen all bird species for seasonal pattern at tumbarumba

```{r}

# ============================================================
# Tumbarumba: seasonal vocal activity across bird species
# ============================================================

# Scientific investigation
#
# Which bird species exhibit the strongest seasonal patterns
# in vocal activity at Tumbarumba?
#
# Do different species peak at different times of year?
#
# Can we identify promising species for further modelling?
#
# Vocal activity is the proportion of recorded 3-second
# windows containing at least one vocalisation.
#
# This measures acoustic activity, not bird abundance.

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyr)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Identify Tumbarumba species datasets
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Select files associated with Tumbarumba, using their
# filename or the SiteName field.

tumba_species_files <- names(acoustic_data)[
  sapply(names(acoustic_data), function(file) {
    data <- acoustic_data[[file]]

    grepl("Tumbarumba", file, ignore.case = TRUE) ||
      ("SiteName" %in% names(data) &&
         any(grepl("Tumbarumba", data$SiteName,
                   ignore.case = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE))
  })
]

cat("\nTumbarumba species datasets:",
    length(tumba_species_files), "\n")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Combine species acoustic records
# ------------------------------------------------------------

tumba_all_birds <- bind_rows(
  lapply(tumba_species_files, function(file) {

    data <- acoustic_data[[file]]

    # Identify the recording date column.

    date_column <- grep(
      "date|timestamp|eventstart|recorded",
      names(data),
      ignore.case = TRUE,
      value = TRUE
    )[1]

    # Use the scientific name supplied in the dataset.

    dates <- as.Date(
      parse_date_time(
        as.character(data[[date_column]]),
        orders = c(
          "ymd HMS", "ymd HM", "ymd",
          "dmy HMS", "dmy HM", "dmy"
        ),
        quiet = TRUE
      )
    )

    data.frame(
      species = data$ScientificName,
      site = data$SiteName,
      date = dates,
      vocal_windows = as.numeric(
        data[["number of 3-sec windows with ≥1 vocalisation"]]
      ),
      total_windows = as.numeric(
        data[["total 3-sec windows recorded that day"]]
      )
    )
  })
) %>%
  filter(
    grepl("Tumbarumba", site, ignore.case = TRUE),
    !is.na(date),
    !is.na(species),
    !is.na(vocal_windows),
    !is.na(total_windows),
    total_windows > 0,
    vocal_windows >= 0,
    vocal_windows <= total_windows
  ) %>%
  mutate(calendar_month = month(date))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Calculate monthly vocal activity for each species
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Pool observations from the same calendar month
# across all available years.
#
# Sum vocalisation-positive windows and total windows
# before calculating activity, so recording effort is
# accounted for.

tumba_species_seasonal <- tumba_all_birds %>%
  group_by(species, calendar_month) %>%
  summarise(
    vocal_windows = sum(vocal_windows),
    total_windows = sum(total_windows),
    vocal_activity = 100 * vocal_windows / total_windows,
    days_sampled = n_distinct(date),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Standardise activity within each species
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Z-scores show whether a month has higher or lower
# activity than that species' own annual monthly mean.
#
# This makes seasonal patterns comparable across species
# with very different overall vocal activity levels.

tumba_species_seasonal <- tumba_species_seasonal %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  mutate(
    seasonal_sd = sd(vocal_activity),
    standardised_activity = if_else(
      !is.na(seasonal_sd) & seasonal_sd > 0,
      (vocal_activity - mean(vocal_activity)) / seasonal_sd,
      0
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Plot seasonal vocal activity heatmap
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_heatmap <- ggplot(
  tumba_species_seasonal,
  aes(
    x = calendar_month,
    y = species,
    fill = standardised_activity
  )
) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:12,
    labels = month.abb,
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "steelblue",
    mid = "white",
    high = "firebrick",
    midpoint = 0,
    name = "Relative\nactivity"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Seasonal bird vocal activity at Tumbarumba",
    subtitle = "Monthly activity standardised within each species",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Species"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(colour = "black"),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

print(p_heatmap)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Rank species by seasonal variation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Calculate the difference between maximum and minimum
# monthly vocal activity.
#
# This is a descriptive screening measure, not a formal
# statistical test of seasonality.

tumba_seasonal_ranking <- tumba_species_seasonal %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    months = n(),
    peak_month = month.abb[
      calendar_month[which.max(vocal_activity)]
    ],
    minimum_activity = min(vocal_activity),
    maximum_activity = max(vocal_activity),
    seasonal_range = maximum_activity - minimum_activity,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(seasonal_range))

cat("\nSPECIES RANKED BY SEASONAL VARIATION\n\n")

print(
  tumba_seasonal_ranking,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Questions for interpretation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Which species exhibit pronounced seasonal peaks?
#
# 2. Do species differ in their peak vocal activity month?
#
# 3. Are spring and summer peaks common across species?
#
# 4. Which species show relatively little seasonal variation?
#
# 5. Which species would be most interesting for modelling
#    relationships with environmental anomalies?
#
# IMPORTANT:
# The heatmap shows relative seasonal patterns.
# The ranking uses absolute percentage-point differences,
# so highly vocal species may rank above quieter species.
#
# We must also check temporal coverage and recording
# effort before selecting species for statistical models.

```


```{r}

# ============================================================
# Tumbarumba: common names and seasonal overlap between birds
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Add common names to the species ranking
# ------------------------------------------------------------

bird_names <- data.frame(
  species = c(
    "Eopsaltria australis",
    "Colluricincla harmonica",
    "Rhipidura albiscapa",
    "Pachycephala pectoralis",
    "Caligavis chrysops",
    "Strepera graculina",
    "Cormobates leucophaea",
    "Acanthiza pusilla",
    "Callocephalon fimbriatum",
    "Acanthiza lineata",
    "Dacelo novaeguineae",
    "Zosterops lateralis",
    "Ninox boobook",
    "Coracina novaehollandiae"
  ),
  common_name = c(
    "Eastern Yellow Robin",
    "Grey Shrikethrush",
    "Grey Fantail",
    "Golden Whistler",
    "Yellow-faced Honeyeater",
    "Pied Currawong",
    "White-throated Treecreeper",
    "Brown Thornbill",
    "Gang-gang Cockatoo",
    "Striated Thornbill",
    "Laughing Kookaburra",
    "Silvereye",
    "Southern Boobook",
    "Black-faced Cuckooshrike"
  )
)

tumba_seasonal_ranking_named <- tumba_seasonal_ranking %>%
  left_join(bird_names, by = "species") %>%
  select(
    common_name, species, months, peak_month,
    minimum_activity, maximum_activity, seasonal_range
  )

cat("\nSEASONAL RANKING WITH COMMON NAMES\n\n")

print(tumba_seasonal_ranking_named, n = Inf, width = Inf)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Calculate seasonal correlation between species
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Each species has 12 monthly vocal activity values.
# Pearson correlation measures similarity in their
# seasonal patterns, not similarity in overall activity.

seasonal_wide <- tumba_species_seasonal %>%
  select(species, calendar_month, vocal_activity) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = species,
    values_from = vocal_activity
  ) %>%
  arrange(calendar_month)

seasonal_correlations <- cor(
  seasonal_wide %>% select(-calendar_month),
  use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
  method = "pearson"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Display a seasonal similarity heatmap
# ------------------------------------------------------------

correlation_plot_data <- as.data.frame(
  as.table(seasonal_correlations)
) %>%
  rename(
    species_1 = Var1,
    species_2 = Var2,
    correlation = Freq
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    bird_names,
    by = c("species_1" = "species")
  ) %>%
  rename(bird_1 = common_name) %>%
  left_join(
    bird_names,
    by = c("species_2" = "species")
  ) %>%
  rename(bird_2 = common_name)

p_overlap <- ggplot(
  correlation_plot_data,
  aes(x = bird_1, y = bird_2, fill = correlation)
) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "steelblue",
    mid = "white",
    high = "firebrick",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-1, 1),
    name = "Seasonal\ncorrelation"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Similarity in seasonal bird vocal activity",
    subtitle = "Pearson correlations across 12 calendar months",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45, hjust = 1, colour = "black"
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black"),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

print(p_overlap)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Identify the most similar and contrasting species pairs
# ------------------------------------------------------------

species_pairs <- correlation_plot_data %>%
  filter(as.character(species_1) < as.character(species_2)) %>%
  select(bird_1, bird_2, correlation) %>%
  arrange(desc(correlation))

cat("\nMOST SIMILAR SEASONAL PATTERNS\n\n")
print(head(species_pairs, 10))

cat("\nMOST CONTRASTING SEASONAL PATTERNS\n\n")
print(tail(species_pairs, 10) %>% arrange(correlation))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Compare overlap in the three highest-activity months
# ------------------------------------------------------------

top_months <- tumba_species_seasonal %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  slice_max(
    order_by = vocal_activity,
    n = 3,
    with_ties = FALSE
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(bird_names, by = "species") %>%
  arrange(common_name, desc(vocal_activity))

top_month_overlap <- top_months %>%
  select(species, calendar_month) %>%
  inner_join(
    top_months %>%
      select(species, calendar_month),
    by = "calendar_month",
    suffix = c("_1", "_2")
  ) %>%
  filter(species_1 < species_2) %>%
  count(species_1, species_2, name = "shared_peak_months") %>%
  right_join(
    expand_grid(
      species_1 = unique(top_months$species),
      species_2 = unique(top_months$species)
    ) %>%
      filter(species_1 < species_2),
    by = c("species_1", "species_2")
  ) %>%
  mutate(shared_peak_months = replace_na(shared_peak_months, 0L)) %>%
  left_join(bird_names, by = c("species_1" = "species")) %>%
  rename(bird_1 = common_name) %>%
  left_join(bird_names, by = c("species_2" = "species")) %>%
  rename(bird_2 = common_name) %>%
  select(bird_1, bird_2, shared_peak_months) %>%
  arrange(desc(shared_peak_months), bird_1, bird_2)

cat("\nSPECIES PAIRS SHARING ALL THREE PEAK MONTHS\n\n")

print(
  top_month_overlap %>%
    filter(shared_peak_months == 3),
  n = Inf
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Interpretation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Correlation close to +1:
# Species have similar annual patterns of vocal activity.
#
# Correlation close to -1:
# Species tend to be most vocal at different times of year.
#
# Three shared peak months:
# Species have the same three highest-activity months,
# although their order and magnitude may differ.
#
# These are descriptive comparisons, not statistical tests.
# They do not establish shared ecological drivers.
#
# Monthly profiles pool observations across years.
# We should verify comparable recording coverage before
# interpreting species differences biologically.

```


```{r}

# ============================================================
# Tumbarumba: shared vocal activity across seven bird species
# ============================================================

# Research question:
# Do seven species with strongly correlated annual seasonal
# profiles also vary together between individual months
# and years?
#
# We first remove each species' usual calendar-month
# pattern, then compare the remaining variation.

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Select all seven species
# ------------------------------------------------------------

selected_birds <- c(
  "Colluricincla harmonica",
  "Cormobates leucophaea",
  "Pachycephala pectoralis",
  "Caligavis chrysops",
  "Rhipidura albiscapa",
  "Ninox boobook",
  "Eopsaltria australis"
)

bird_labels <- c(
  "Colluricincla harmonica" = "Grey Shrikethrush",
  "Cormobates leucophaea" = "White-throated Treecreeper",
  "Pachycephala pectoralis" = "Golden Whistler",
  "Caligavis chrysops" = "Yellow-faced Honeyeater",
  "Rhipidura albiscapa" = "Grey Fantail",
  "Ninox boobook" = "Southern Boobook",
  "Eopsaltria australis" = "Eastern Yellow Robin"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Calculate monthly vocal activity
# ------------------------------------------------------------

bird_monthly <- tumba_all_birds %>%
  filter(species %in% selected_birds) %>%
  mutate(month = floor_date(date, "month")) %>%
  group_by(species, month) %>%
  summarise(
    vocal_windows = sum(vocal_windows),
    total_windows = sum(total_windows),
    recording_days = n_distinct(date),
    vocal_activity = 100 * vocal_windows / total_windows,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    common_name = unname(bird_labels[species]),
    calendar_month = lubridate::month(month)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Check recording coverage
# ------------------------------------------------------------

coverage_summary <- bird_monthly %>%
  group_by(common_name) %>%
  summarise(
    first_month = min(month),
    last_month = max(month),
    months_recorded = n(),
    recording_days = sum(recording_days),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("\nRECORDING COVERAGE\n\n")
print(coverage_summary, n = Inf, width = Inf)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Retain months shared by all seven species
# ------------------------------------------------------------

shared_months <- bird_monthly %>%
  count(month, name = "species_recorded") %>%
  filter(species_recorded == length(selected_birds)) %>%
  pull(month)

bird_shared <- bird_monthly %>%
  filter(month %in% shared_months) %>%
  arrange(species, month)

cat("\nMONTHS SHARED BY ALL SEVEN SPECIES:",
    length(shared_months), "\n")

if (length(shared_months) > 0) {
  cat("First shared month:",
      as.character(min(shared_months)), "\n")
  cat("Last shared month:",
      as.character(max(shared_months)), "\n")

  complete_months <- seq(
    min(shared_months),
    max(shared_months),
    by = "month"
  )

  missing_months <- setdiff(complete_months, shared_months)

  cat("Missing calendar months within shared period:",
      length(missing_months), "\n")

  if (length(missing_months) > 0) {
    print(as.Date(missing_months))
  }
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Calculate species-specific seasonal anomalies
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# For each species, subtract its mean activity for
# the corresponding calendar month across shared years.
#
# Example:
# November 2016 activity minus that species' average
# November activity.
#
# Positive = more vocal than usual for that month.
# Negative = less vocal than usual for that month.

bird_anomalies <- bird_shared %>%
  group_by(species, calendar_month) %>%
  mutate(
    monthly_baseline = mean(vocal_activity),
    activity_anomaly = vocal_activity - monthly_baseline
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Plot year-to-year vocal activity anomalies
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_bird_anomalies <- ggplot(
  bird_anomalies,
  aes(x = month, y = activity_anomaly)
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey50"
  ) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue", size = 1.1) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ common_name,
    ncol = 1,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Interannual variation in bird vocal activity",
    subtitle = "Anomalies relative to each species' usual calendar-month activity",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Vocal activity anomaly (percentage points)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(colour = "black"),
    strip.text = element_text(colour = "black")
  )

print(p_bird_anomalies)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Correlate anomalies between species
# ------------------------------------------------------------

anomaly_wide <- bird_anomalies %>%
  select(month, common_name, activity_anomaly) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = common_name,
    values_from = activity_anomaly
  ) %>%
  arrange(month)

anomaly_correlations <- cor(
  anomaly_wide %>% select(-month),
  use = "complete.obs",
  method = "pearson"
)

cat("\nCORRELATIONS BETWEEN MONTHLY VOCAL ACTIVITY ANOMALIES\n\n")
print(round(anomaly_correlations, 3))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Summarise correlations between species pairs
# ------------------------------------------------------------

anomaly_pairs <- as.data.frame(
  as.table(anomaly_correlations)
) %>%
  rename(
    bird_1 = Var1,
    bird_2 = Var2,
    correlation = Freq
  ) %>%
  filter(as.character(bird_1) < as.character(bird_2)) %>%
  arrange(desc(correlation))

cat("\nSPECIES PAIRS RANKED BY ANOMALY CORRELATION\n\n")
print(anomaly_pairs, n = Inf)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Interpretation questions
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. How many months of data overlap across all seven birds?
#
# 2. Do the birds have unusually high or low vocal activity
#    in the same months and years?
#
# 3. Which species pairs remain strongly correlated after
#    their average seasonal cycles have been removed?
#
# 4. Are any species behaving independently of the others?
#
# 5. Could environmental anomalies explain the remaining
#    shared variation?
#
# IMPORTANT:
# These correlations are descriptive and do not establish
# common environmental drivers.
#
# The next stage will test temperature and soil moisture
# relationships while accounting for species and season.

```
